_readme: REWARD LEVER INVENTORY — DAVID OWNS THIS FILE (R8; same doctrine as signal_lenses.json). The named mechanisms that exist in UK reward practice, surfaced in an Options block beside a gap — NEVER ranked, scored, starred or ordered by fit (file order only; an ordered list is an implied recommendation). Every lever carries a trade_off — a lever with no stated downside is marketing. No vendor, provider or product is ever named. register_effect says which register the lever moves: 'Substance' (position/provision — what you offer or how much) or 'Approach' (practice — how you operate); a member behind on POSITION needs a Substance lever, one CONTRADICTED on practice needs an Approach lever. typical_shape is domain knowledge unless prevalence_metric_id links a measured metric (then peer take-up renders live). v1 tranche per R8: Pay, Benefits & Lifestyle, Time Off & Family (the three densest evidence categories); Governance is the ruled second tranche. STATUS: drafted 2026-08-14 — pending David's content sign-off; refine, reject or extend freely.

levers.name: Formal pay bands with published progression
levers.what_it_is: Defined salary ranges per grade, with the rules for moving through them written down.
levers.typical_shape: Bands built from survey data around a target market position, refreshed annually; progression tied to a documented mechanism.
levers.trade_off: Bands surface every existing anomaly the day they are shared — budget for correction cases before, not after.

levers.name: Merit matrix for the annual review
levers.what_it_is: Pay increases set by the combination of performance rating and position in range.
levers.typical_shape: A published grid; higher increases for strong performers low in range, tapering at range maximum.
levers.trade_off: Only as credible as the performance ratings feeding it — rating inflation quietly flattens the differentiation it promises.

levers.name: Pay-for-skills premiums
levers.what_it_is: Defined premiums for named scarce skills or certifications, separate from the base structure.
levers.typical_shape: A short list of premium-bearing skills reviewed each year; premiums lapse when scarcity does.
levers.trade_off: Premiums are easy to grant and politically hard to remove once the scarcity passes.

levers.name: Targeted adjustment pot
levers.what_it_is: A ring-fenced slice of the review budget for correcting specific market or equity gaps rather than spreading it evenly.
levers.typical_shape: A minority share of the annual budget held back and allocated case-by-case against benchmark evidence.
levers.trade_off: Everyone not in the pot gets a smaller flat award that year — the fairness story has to be told, not assumed.

levers.name: Flexible benefits allowance
levers.what_it_is: A per-employee allowance spent across a menu of benefits instead of one fixed package.
levers.typical_shape: A core of protected benefits plus a flexible allowance; enrolment windows once or twice a year.
levers.trade_off: Platform and administration costs are real and permanent; take-up disappoints where communication is thin.

levers.name: Salary-sacrifice arrangements
levers.what_it_is: Benefits funded from gross pay — pension, cars, technology — sharing the NI saving between employer and employee.
levers.typical_shape: Pension by default, with car and technology schemes added where the workforce profile suits.
levers.trade_off: Lower-paid employees near the wage floor may be unable to participate — the benefit lands unevenly by design.

levers.name: Group risk bundle
levers.what_it_is: Life assurance, income protection and critical illness bought together as an insured bundle.
levers.typical_shape: Life cover for all staff with income protection layered on for salaried populations.
levers.trade_off: Premiums re-rate with claims experience and workforce age — the cost is not fixed at purchase.

levers.name: Voluntary benefits platform
levers.what_it_is: Employee-paid benefits at group rates — discounts, insurance top-ups, financial products — at low employer cost.
levers.typical_shape: A discounts core with optional employee-funded insurances alongside.
levers.trade_off: Perceived value is far below paid benefits — it widens choice, it does not read as investment.

levers.name: Enhanced family leave
levers.what_it_is: Maternity, paternity and adoption pay above the statutory floor.
levers.typical_shape: A stepped enhancement — a period at full pay, then a period at half pay, service-gated.
levers.trade_off: Effectively irreversible — withdrawing family pay reads as bad faith, so the commitment is permanent from day one.

levers.name: Holiday purchase / sale
levers.what_it_is: Employees buy or sell a capped number of leave days through payroll.
levers.typical_shape: Up to a week each way, elected once a year alongside benefits enrolment.
levers.trade_off: Payroll and accrual administration is fiddly, and heavy selling can quietly signal an overwork problem.

levers.name: Occupational sick pay above SSP
levers.what_it_is: Company sick pay for a defined period before statutory rates apply.
levers.typical_shape: Service-banded full-pay then half-pay periods, with absence triggers managed alongside.
levers.trade_off: Costs concentrate in the highest-absence populations, and tightening a scheme later is far harder than never enhancing it.

levers.name: Paid carer's leave
levers.what_it_is: Paid time off for caring responsibilities beyond the statutory unpaid entitlement.
levers.typical_shape: A small number of paid days a year, claimed without evidence requirements.
levers.trade_off: Low headline cost but hard to forecast — usage is invisible until the policy exists.
